# Requirements-Quality Checklist: In-App Feedback

**Purpose**: Review the approved in-app-feedback specification and planning artifacts for completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and release readiness before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-08-25
**Feature**: [In-App Feedback specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Authentication and authorization

- [x] CHK001 Are authenticated-only opening and submission boundaries explicitly specified, including the behavior for an unauthenticated request? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK002 Is “every protected area” reconciled with the complete protected-route inventory, including workspace, onboarding, and join route families? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Plan §Protected-area placement]
- [x] CHK003 Is the server-derived source of the authenticated identity for abuse control explicit, with no client-supplied identifier accepted for that purpose? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, Plan §Submission boundary and validation]
- [x] CHK004 Are the source, eligibility condition, and sole permitted use of a contact email unambiguous: authenticated server session, explicit per-report opt-in, and follow-up only? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Contract §Client form to Server Action]
- [x] CHK005 Are authorization boundaries for the limiter and its administrative cleanup sufficiently specified to support least-privilege evidence rather than application-only assurance? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check II, Data Model §Feedback submission limit]

## Privacy and data minimization

- [x] CHK006 Is the external administrative-delivery payload enumerated exhaustively enough to distinguish each allowed value from all excluded context? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008–FR-010, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency]
- [x] CHK007 Are prohibited automatic context categories explicit and consistent across the specification, contract, and delivery plan? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, Contract §Client form to Server Action]
- [x] CHK008 Is the prohibition on feedback content and opted-in email entering ordinary logs or diagnostics explicit for every documented failure category? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, Plan §Failure semantics]
- [x] CHK009 Is limiter processing bounded to the stated abuse-prevention purpose, with analytics and tracking explicitly excluded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, Plan §Abuse-control semantics and cleanup]
- [x] CHK010 Are the third-party processing boundaries for Resend and the administrative inbox named without prematurely assigning legal roles? [Consistency, Plan §Release Configuration and Documentation]
- [x] CHK011 Are release-review topics for the external channel complete enough to cover provider/dashboard retention, DPA, subprocessors, account/usage data, termination deletion, transfers, and inbox access/retention/deletion? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Plan §Release Configuration and Documentation]
- [x] CHK012 Is the requirement to disable Resend open/click tracking stated as a release gate in addition to plaintext delivery, rather than inferred from the absence of tracking fields? [Clarity, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Quickstart §Validation scenarios]

## Data lifecycle

- [x] CHK013 Is the maximum physical retention lifecycle for each limiter field objectively bounded, including the hourly cleanup margin? [Measurability, Plan §Abuse-control semantics and cleanup, Data Model §Feedback submission limit]
- [x] CHK014 Are account-deletion semantics for the limiter explicit as hard deletion, distinct from expiry cleanup? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check IV, Data Model §Feedback submission limit]
- [x] CHK015 Is the scheduled-cleanup dependency documented with enabling, deployment verification, failure monitoring, upgrade recovery, and job-history maintenance expectations? [Completeness, Plan §Abuse-control semantics and cleanup, Research §Cron job history]
- [x] CHK016 Is the no-persistence boundary for feedback text, pathname, and opted-in contact data in Cadence consistent with every data-model and delivery statement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, Data Model §Feedback submission]
- [x] CHK017 Is external provider and administrative-inbox lifecycle review explicitly a pre-release human gate, rather than an automated or assumed guarantee? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, Plan §Release Configuration and Documentation]

## Abuse control

- [x] CHK018 Is the three-attempt rule unambiguously defined as a 24-hour window anchored at the first valid attempt, rather than a rolling or sliding window? [Clarity, Plan §Abuse-control semantics and cleanup]
- [x] CHK019 Are validation-failure conditions and their non-consumption of a limiter slot stated consistently in the requirements, data model, and failure semantics? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Plan §Failure semantics, Data Model §Feedback submission limit]
- [x] CHK020 Is consumption after successful validation and atomic slot acquisition unambiguously retained for provider rejection, ambiguous transport failure, and unexpected delivery failure? [Completeness, Plan §Abuse-control semantics and cleanup]
- [x] CHK021 Is the same-key ambiguous retry explicitly included in the definition of a slot-consuming valid attempt? [Clarity, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Data Model §Feedback submission limit]
- [x] CHK022 Is the fourth valid-attempt outcome specified without disclosing limiter details that would materially assist evasion? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Data Model §Feedback submission limit]
- [x] CHK023 Are atomicity and concurrent-attempt requirements expressed at a database-enforced verification layer, with an objectively defined maximum of three slots? [Measurability, Plan §Constitution Check I and V]

## Delivery and idempotency

- [x] CHK024 Is provider acceptance, rather than inbox arrival, reading, or human acknowledgement, consistently defined as the sole success boundary? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency]
- [x] CHK025 Are definitive provider rejection, ambiguous transport failure, and provider idempotency conflict distinguished adequately for recovery rules while preserving a shared safe user-facing failure? [Completeness, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Plan §Failure semantics]
- [x] CHK026 Is “canonical provider payload unchanged” sufficiently defined to include type, trimmed message, normalized pathname, follow-up choice, and every other Resend-request value? [Clarity, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Contract §Server Action result]
- [x] CHK027 Is the new-key requirement after any payload-relevant change consistent with the permitted same-key retry rule? [Consistency, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Research §Resend delivery and idempotency]
- [x] CHK028 Is the idempotency-key requirement explicit that the random UUID contains no PII or financial data and is neither logged nor persisted as feedback history? [Completeness, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Data Model §Feedback submission]
- [x] CHK029 Is the idempotency-conflict outcome specified as generic and non-successful, without exposing provider details? [Clarity, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Contract §Server Action result]

## Failure semantics

- [x] CHK030 Are validation failure, abuse rejection, provider rejection, ambiguous transport failure, and unexpected internal failure each specified with their slot-consumption and retry/content-retention consequences? [Completeness, Plan §Failure semantics]
- [x] CHK031 Are user-facing failure messages constrained to avoid provider/internal details and false success claims in every failure category? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011 and FR-014, Plan §Failure semantics]
- [x] CHK032 Is entered-content retention after field validation failure and delivery failure defined clearly enough to support the idempotent-retry rules without retaining content beyond the client interaction? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 4, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency]
- [x] CHK033 Is the success condition excluded from timed-out, interrupted, and otherwise unconfirmed delivery outcomes? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, Plan §Failure semantics]

## Accessibility and user experience

- [x] CHK034 Are keyboard operation, dialog semantics, focus restoration, and accessible status/error announcements explicitly required rather than merely inferred from reuse of existing patterns? [Completeness, Plan §Protected-area placement, Quickstart §Validation scenarios]
- [x] CHK035 Is responsive placement specified for both workspace-shell mobile navigation and protected routes outside that shell, including a measurable viewport or safe-area expectation where needed? [Clarity, Plan §Protected-area placement, Quickstart §Validation scenarios]
- [x] CHK036 Are sensitive-data warning requirements visible before submission and sufficiently specific about passwords, banking information, credentials, and other sensitive information? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK037 Are the type-specific prompts for bug reports and suggestions explicit enough to distinguish observed-versus-expected behavior from desired improvement guidance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004–FR-005]
- [x] CHK038 Is the under-two-minute MVP completion criterion scoped to an identifiable acceptance scenario without implying a formal moderated usability study? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]

## Testability and evidence

- [x] CHK039 Does every critical requirement identify a suitable verification layer—pure/unit, database compliance, browser acceptance, or human release review—without conflating them? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check, Quickstart §Validation scenarios]
- [x] CHK040 Are database authorization, atomic limiter, expiry deletion, and account deletion requirements explicitly reserved for database/hosted compliance evidence rather than application-only mocks? [Consistency, Constitution §V, Plan §Constitution Check I and V]
- [x] CHK041 Is the prohibition on contacting Resend from automated tests explicit while deterministic provider-payload and outcome coverage remains specified? [Clarity, Plan §Technical Context, Quickstart §Prerequisites and Validation scenarios]
- [x] CHK042 Are same-key/same-payload, changed-payload/new-key, same-key slot consumption, and idempotency-conflict requirements each traceable to deterministic test coverage? [Traceability, Plan §Resend delivery and idempotency, Quickstart §Validation scenarios]
- [x] CHK043 Are human release gates—provider/inbox lifecycle, legal-role review, sender-domain tracking configuration, and operational cron review—clearly separated from automated acceptance criteria? [Completeness, Plan §Release Configuration and Documentation, Quickstart §Validation scenarios]

## Constitution alignment and task-generation readiness

- [x] CHK044 Does the plan identify whether and how the feature affects all five Cadence Constitution principles, with corresponding evidence and durable-contract updates? [Completeness, Constitution §I–V, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [x] CHK045 Are the limiter’s non-workspace personal-security metadata treatment and its RLS/least-privilege approach reconciled with the Constitution’s tenant-isolation and authenticated-access principles? [Consistency, Constitution §I–II, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [x] CHK046 Are the planned updates to data handling, deletion, portability, and LGPD mapping adequate to prevent a duplicate or contradictory durable privacy/lifecycle contract? [Consistency, Constitution §III–IV, Plan §Release Configuration and Documentation]
- [x] CHK047 Are all marked human-review dependencies explicitly release-gating and sufficiently bounded that task generation can proceed without reopening settled product or architecture decisions? [Readiness, Spec §FR-015, Plan §Release Configuration and Documentation]
- [x] CHK048 Has the review confirmed that no actual contradiction, omission, or untestable critical invariant remains that must be resolved before tasks are generated? [Readiness, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add findings or resolution notes inline, including links to the affected artifact.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
